description: Athlete is on injury hold for IT band inflammation, race 8 weeks away. Asks what they can do. Dean must give specific cross-training guidance that preserves fitness without IT band stress.

user.name: Priya
user.injury_notes: IT band inflammation — left knee. On rest per physio since May 4. Race is 8 weeks away.

recent_conversation.content: IT band at mile 8 on an 11-miler — that's the classic overuse pattern. Rest it fully for 3-5 days, no running. If you have a physio, get in as soon as you can. Keep icing if it's tender. I'll hold the plan until we know more.
Saw my physio — she said IT band is inflamed, no running for at least a week. Going to be careful.
Good call going in. Complete rest from running for now. 8 weeks to your half is enough time to recover and still race well — we're not behind yet. Check back in at the end of the week.

inbound_sms: Day 6 of no running and it's killing me. Knee is feeling a lot better though. What can I actually do to stay in shape without making it worse?

ground_truth.notes: Athlete is on an active injury hold (injury_hold_since set, weekly_mileage_target=0). She's asking for cross-training options while on hold — this is the RIGHT question to answer. Dean MUST: (1) keep plan_action.injury_hold active (IT band not cleared yet); (2) give 2-3 SPECIFIC cross-training options that are safe for IT band — pool running/aqua jogging is the gold standard (near-zero IT band stress), cycling is borderline (some IT band loading) so mention it with a caveat, elliptical is generally okay. Name them specifically; (3) note that pool running at effort preserves aerobic fitness better than pure rest; (4) reinforce the 8-week timeline is still workable. A response that just says 'pool or bike' without explaining WHY those work for IT band scores below 7. A response that suggests any running scores 0. The cross-training specificity is the key criterion.
